To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

vitamin D, and/or its active metabolite, may have a beneficial impact on insulin sensitivity in humans, and that the mechanism of action may be through a direct effect on insulin action or through indirect effects on insulin release and body fat.

vitamin D status is associated with insulin sensitivity and this relationship may be mediated by several factors, including lean mass, insulin secretion, insulin receptor expression and parathyroid hormone status.

vitamin D status is inversely associated to insulin sensitivity, even when glucose metabolism parameters are classified as normal, in epidemiological studies and in intervention studies, and that this effect is mediated by several mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vitamin D in insulin sensitivity.
the role of vitamin D in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance, and the potential for vitamin D supplementation as a means of preventing or delaying the development of type 2 diabetes.
the effects of vitamin D on insulin sensitivity, and we have identified a number of potential pathways by which vitamin D may exert its beneficial effects on glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

vitamin D status, as assessed by 25(OH)D, is inversely related to diabetes risk and that vitamin D supplementation, at doses that are not associated with hypercalcaemia, may have the potential to prevent diabetes in at-risk individuals and to improve insulin sensitivity in subjects with prediabetes and diabetes.
vitamin D is an emerging nutrient of interest for its potential to improve insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism.
vitamin D supplementation may improve insulin sensitivity in subjects with low vitamin D status, although the mechanisms underlying this relationship remain to be fully elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin D status is inversely associated to insulin sensitivity, but that the mechanisms are not fully elucidated.
vitamin D status may have a role in the prevention or treatment of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes and may have a role to play in the prevention of the metabolic syndrome.
vitamin D deficiency may play a role in the development of insulin resistance and diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an emerging role for vitamin D in insulin sensitivity and that this relationship is independent of calcium and phosphorus metabolism.
vitamin D status is inversely related to insulin sensitivity, which has implications for the prevention of prediabetes, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
vitamin D may play a critical role in the prevention of diabetes and the treatment of diabetes.
